title: USMNT duo Brenden Aaronson and Chris Richards suffer injury scares 26 days before World Cup opener
content:
U.S. defender Chris Richards and midfielder Brenden Aaronson both suffered injury scares on the penultimate Sunday of the English Premier League season, though both appear to have avoided major setbacks.

A week before U.S. men’s national team coach Mauricio Pochettino names his World Cup roster, Richards landed awkwardly on his ankle after an aerial duel while playing for Crystal Palace against Brentford, and Aaronson was replaced in the 59th minute after going down with what Leeds manager Daniel Farke said was a “dead leg” during his side’s victory over Brighton & Hove Albion.

Farke and Palace manager Oliver Glasner both seemed to indicate that the injuries to their American players were minor.

Glasner admitted he was “a little bit more concerned” about Richards than some other Palace players. “He twisted his ankle,” the Austrian coach said. “It is quite swollen, so we will have to assess it further. But hopefully he can return midweek.

Palace face Rayo Vallecano in the Europa Conference League final on May 27, three days after the Premier League season finishes on May 24.

Farke, meanwhile, said after Leeds’ 1-0 win over Brighton that he was “more optimistic” about Aaronson’s condition than about German midfielder Anton Stach, who was taken off on a stretcher 15 minutes after Aaronson left the match.

“It was just a dead leg,” Farke said of Aaronson’s injury. “He was, even at halftime, on the bike trying to keep going. It normally just lasts a few days, but it was getting tighter and tighter. He should be alright for the next game.”

Some 20 minutes after Aaronson went down, so did Richards. Having entered Sunday’s match at Brentford in the 61st minute as a substitute, Richards jumped with Igor Thiago for a header and landed awkwardly.

He immediately crumpled to the ground in pain. As medical staff tended to him, Glasner readied a substitute. But Richards, after a minute on the sideline, re-entered the match and completed it.

Of the two players, Richards is the integral one. He is one of the first names in U.S. head coach Mauricio Pochettino’s starting lineup, and arguably the USMNT’s only reliable center back.

If the ankle injury were to impact his World Cup participation, an already-thin position for the U.S. would get even thinner.

It’s unclear when exactly Aaronson suffered the dead leg. Up until the 56th minute, he appeared to be moving reasonably well. But in the 57th, he began visibly struggling, bereft of the energy that typically defines his game. And in the 58th, he sank to the pitch and called for medical attention.

After discussions with medical staff and manual tests on his left leg, Aaronson then limped off the field and was replaced.

He was not distraught, but did look concerned and in discomfort as he headed toward the bench.

Aaronson, 25, is expected to be among the 26 players named to the U.S. World Cup squad on May 26. He has not been a regular starter for the USMNT in years, but his relatively strong season at Leeds has put him in contention for minutes this summer.

If healthy, he is a candidate for a role similar to the one he played at the 2022 World Cup, when he brought energy as a second-half substitute.

If the dead leg were to impact his World Cup participation, it would be a blow on a personal level, but the U.S. has plenty of depth in attacking midfield areas.
